post.description:
Indexes are created on a per _**Aggregate Config**_ basis. This means that each aggregate will have its own index and when listing and searching, for performance purposes, the search is limited to the aggregate's index.

_**If you wish to search on a specific property of the aggregate, it needs to be specified in the**_ _**`indexKey`**_ _**array in the aggregate's config. This includes the**_ _**`range`**_ _**property which will only work if the**_ _**`prop`**_ _**is indexed**_

We don't index the whole aggregate, only the fields that are specified in the config. The index provides a pointer to the aggregate, so when querying, we get a list of aggregate subject and topics and then go and get those to return in the search results.

Properties listed in the `indexKey` section of the config will result in that property being indexed. The property along with the subject and topic will be stored in the index. This gives us a pointer to the aggregate.

We also store a timestamp (`aggregateTimestamp`) on the index. This value is used for sorting results. Basically, if no sort preferences are present in the query, then the default sort will be by the timestamp descending.

`from` - can be used to page your results, meaning you can specify where in the list you want to start the results from.

`size` - how many results to return. If no value is provided, it will default to 100. The maximum it will allow is 1000. If you want more than 1000 rows returned, then you will need to make multiple requests and change the `from` property to page the results.

`fields` - this is a string array of the `indexKeys` you want to search across. Leave it empty to search across all of them.

`searchTerm` - you can limit the results by providing a search term. Leave empty to return all aggregates for the specified config topic.

`exact` - whether or not the result has to match exactly to be considered a hit.

`sort` - This can be either a property of `{order: 'asc' || 'des'}` or it can be an array of index keys and a direction. `[{"Email": {"order: "asc"}}, ...]`

`range` - this allows you to filter the results between a range of values. It is important to note that you can only specify a property to filter on that is contained within the index. `prop` is the property of the aggregate that you want to filter (must be indexed), `before` can be an ISO formatted date string or milliseconds and will return all that equal or are before the value. `after` is the same and will filter all that are equal or after the value.

`version` - you can provide the version as an epoch number or an ISO Date string. The returned list will contain only those results as they were at that point in time. The total value will still show the result count as it is at the current point of time and this will probably differ from the result count of those returned.

post.description: Create contract from answer update config

#### Submit an array of events to the batch handler
When this endpoint is posted to, as long as it is a valid configuration it will always return 200 "Accepted". This means the event has been written to stream, but doesn't guarantee success on the collation run. If the stream is down, it will automatically replay all accepted events when it comes back up.
Incorrect submission shapes will return a 502 "internal server error".

The `productId` and `name` must match the configuration you are trying to invoke.
The Payload array can be made up of any number of objects. The lambda will scale according to the number of objects submitted under a single post.
More data can be submitted that listed below, however these will not be mapped into a quote so will not have any bearing on the quote unless the configuration is updated.

```
loan:
    type:object
    properties:
        account_number: string(required)
        amount: 
            type: integer(required)
            description: The value of the loan in cents
        term_in_months:
            type: integer(required)
            description: The number of the loan term in months
        monthly_repayment:
            type: integer(required)
            description: The value of the monthly repayment of the loan in cents
        settlement_date_time:
            type:string(required)
            format:date-time
        purpose:
            type:array
            items:
                type: string
                enum: [CAR_PURCHASE, CAR_REPAIR, DEBT_CONSOLIDATION, EDUCATIONAL_EXPENSE, HOME_IMPROVEMENT, HOUSEHOLD_FURNISHING, OTHER_VEHICLE_PURCHASE, SMALL_DEBT, TRAVEL, OTHER, REFINANCE, MEDICAL/DENTAL]
        type:
            type: string(required)
            enum: [SINGLE, JOINT]
        dsm:
            type: string(optional)
            enum: [FAST, '']
            description: This triggers a different email marketing parth with sped up timelines to allow for faster testing of marketing materials
applicant1:
    type:object
    properties:
        customerId: string(optional),
        first_name: string(required),
        last_name: string(required),
        address:
            type:object
            properties:
                unit_number: string(optional)
                street_number: string(required)
                street_name: string(required)
                street_type: string(required)
                suburb: string(required)
                state:
                    type: string
                    enum: [WA, NSW, VIC, QLD, SA, WA, TAS, NT, ACT]
                postcode: string(required)
                country: string(optional)
        gender: 
            type: string(required)
            enum[MALE, FEMALE]
        date_of_birth: 
            type:string(required)
            format:date-time
        email: 
            type:string(required)
            format:email
        phone:
            type:object
            properties:
                mobile:
                    type:string(required)
                    description: Mobile phone number with international code. If no international code is present, Evari will transform 04 into +614
                home: string(optional)
                work: string(optional)
        dependents: integer(required)
        primary_employment_type: string(required)
applicant2:
    type:object
    properties:
        customerId: string(optional),
        first_name: string(required),
        last_name: string(required),
        address:
            type:object
            properties:
                unit_number: string(optional)
                street_number: string(required)
                street_name: string(required)
                street_type: string(required)
                suburb: string(required)
                state:
                    type: string
                    enum: [WA, NSW, VIC, QLD, SA, WA, TAS, NT, ACT]
                postcode: string(required)
                country: string(optional)
        gender: 
            type: string(required)
            enum[MALE, FEMALE]
        date_of_birth: 
            type:string(required)
            format:date-time
        email: 
            type:string(required)
            format:email
        phone:
            type:object
            properties:
                mobile:
                    type:string(required)
                    description: Mobile phone number with international code. If no international code is present, Evari will transform 04 into +614
                home: string(optional)
                work: string(optional)
        dependents: integer(required)
        primary_employment_type: string(required)
```

All of the parameters in this example are required.
  • The subject and command are not to be changed.
  • The topic is used to uniquely identify the resource.
    If the same topic is used twice, the first file is overwritten by the second one.
  • The value of base64 should be a valid CSV file that has been encoded to base64.

All of the parameters in this example are required.
  • The topic can be any value.
  • The subject and command are not to be changed.
  • Use the upload topic of your file as the internalKey.

This function removes any property from inside the body object. Any property specified as an empty string (or any string) will be removed (both key and value). Any objects in the request will not be deleted, only empty strings will be removed. 

note: Arrays are overwritten in a normal upsert so it not necessary to use upsert-delete for editing those unless you want to delete the whole array.

IP Whitelisting or a valid bearer token is required to access this endpoint.

BaseUrl environment variable is required to be set in the environment variables for the request to work. The test environment variable is `https://api.puzzle-funding.evari.tech`

`facts` are required to complete the rule calculations. valid facts are shown below for this custom request. Valid values for PACK_GOODS and PACK_CARRIER have been provided to Evari and configured in lookup tables. There is no strict validation enabled on the body or custom `facts`. Missing `facts` will just return a partial result, and addition facts will not be calculated.
``` 
"PACK_CARRIER.value"  - string - the name of the Carrier
"PACK_GOODS.value"  - string - the item to be carried
"DEMO_GOODS_VALUE.value"  - integer - value of item to be insured
"PACK_TRIP_TYPE.value"  - string - type of trip to be insured. (Options are "International Inbound", "Domestic" or "International Outbound")
```
